title: batchDryer operation
description: The drying curve as a batch vessel (choupoBatch): a tray of wet solid losing its moisture into air of DECLARED, CONSTANT condition. The state is the moisture content X = m_moisture / m_drySolid. Above the critical moisture the wetted surface sits at the air's wet-bulb temperature and the flux is gas-film controlled, R_c = k_Y (Y_sat(T_wb) - Y); below it the flux follows the declared characteristic drying curve, R = R_c f(Phi) with Phi = (X - X_eq)/(X_c - X_eq) — linear (f = Phi) when no `dryingCurve` is declared, announced at run time as a modelling CHOICE, not as physics. X_eq is the GAB equilibrium moisture at the air's own water activity, read from the solid component's `sorption {}` record (a solid without one is refused by name). The air is an ENVIRONMENT, not a ledgered stream: the evaporated water leaves the campaign across that boundary and is reported as the unit's declared material residual, and the latent heat — the air's, from outside the campaign — is published as the latentDuty_kW KPI while the energy ledger honestly refuses to claim a verdict.

area.title: Exposed drying area
area.description: Surface of the tray/bed exposed to the air. Equipment data — there is no default.

k_Y.title: Gas-film mass-transfer coefficient
k_Y.description: Mass flux per unit humidity-ratio driving force, kg/(m2 s) per (kg moisture / kg dry gas). SAMPLE/EQUIPMENT data (air velocity, tray geometry) — never defaulted. Declare it dimensionally as `k_Y [1 -2 -1 0 0] <value>;`.

criticalMoisture.title: Critical moisture content X_c
criticalMoisture.description: The break between the constant-rate and the falling-rate periods, on the dry-solid basis. A MEASURED property of this sample, not derivable — and it must lie above the equilibrium moisture X_eq of the declared air, or the falling-rate law has no domain and the unit refuses.

dryingCurve.title: Characteristic drying curve
dryingCurve.description: The shape of the falling-rate period on van Meel's (1958) normalised coordinates: Phi = (X - X_eq)/(X_c - X_eq) and f = R/R_c, so R = R_c f(Phi). Absent, the curve is LINEAR (f = Phi), announced at run time as a modelling choice. `shape power` takes `exponent` n (f = Phi^n; n < 1 keeps the rate high into the falling period, n > 1 drops it early); `shape table` takes two lists `phi` and `f` of the same length, from (0, 0) to (1, 1), phi strictly increasing and f never decreasing, interpolated linearly. A non-linear shape is a claim about THIS material's internal transport and must declare `source` (an article, a dataset, or 'hypothetical teaching curve'); a key that belongs to another shape is refused by name.

moisture.title: Moisture component
moisture.description: Which component is the moisture. Needed only when the tray holds more than one volatile besides the declared carrier — otherwise the single volatile is identified and the ambiguity refusal never fires.

air.title: Declared air environment
air.description: The drying air, declared CONSTANT and not integrated — the FixedBedAdsorber's constant-carrier posture. `T` its temperature [K], `Y` its humidity ratio [kg moisture / kg dry gas], `carrier` the component that is the dry gas (its humid heat and molar mass come from the catalogue; nothing here hardcodes "air"). The wet-bulb temperature and the water activity are RESULTS of this block, never declared.
